claim: Amazon Inspector keeps active findings until they are remediated; it deletes findings 3 days after their resource is deleted, terminated or no longer eligible, and 30 days after they are closed for any other reason.
question: How long does Amazon Inspector keep active and closed findings?
q: docs/inspector/latest/user/findings-understanding

When a resource is deleted, terminated, or no longer eligible for scanning, Amazon Inspector automatically closes findings associated with the resource and then deletes the findings after 3 days. If findings are closed for any other reason, they are deleted after 30 days.
docs/inspector/latest/user/findings-understanding
Amazon Inspector stores all of your active findings until you remediate them.

note: Current truth after the 2024-02 and 2025-06 retention changes.

claim: Detective has a 30-day free trial with the full feature set, during which you can see projected costs for each account, and for all accounts when you use AWS Organizations.
question: How long is the Amazon Detective free trial, and what does it show?
q: www/detective/pricing

You can try Amazon Detective at no additional charge with a 30-day free trial. With the free trial, you get the full Amazon Detective feature set over the 30-day period. During the free trial, you can see projected costs for each account.

q: www/detective/pricing

You are charged per gigabyte (GB) ingested per account/Region/month. There is no additional charge to enable these log sources for analysis or for data stored in Amazon Detective. Amazon Detective maintains up to a year of aggregated data for its analysis.

claim: Detective projects cost by averaging an account's daily data volume over its active days (at most 30) and multiplying the daily average by 30.
question: How does Detective calculate the projected cost shown on its Usage page?
q: docs/detective/latest/userguide/usage-projected-cost-calculation
Multiplies the account's daily average by 30. This is the projected 30-day usage for the account.
